subject: Inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool sizing & flexible commit options
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@optimaai.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@optimaai.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool sizing & flexible commit options

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the intro — we had a quick systems review this morning and want to get an initial sizing + pricing ballpark for a dedicated/reserved pool. High level: we are moving inference for our assistant product to a dedicated setup and need pricing + options for a 12–24 month commit with some flexibility for seasonal bursts.

Quick workload signals:
- Model family: Llama-3-70B (int8 quantized), mostly generation with some few-shot prompts.
- Average request: ~1200 tokens (prompt + expected generation).
- Peak context length: up to 3,500 tokens for some complex multi-turn flows.
- Steady-state request volume: ~25 requests/sec (p50) with 90th percentile bursts to ~140 req/s for 15–30 minute windows.
- Concurrency target for p95 latency SLO: ~60 concurrent requests.
- Latency objective: p95 <= 250 ms for typical responses (we can accept higher for the very long context cases).
- Embeddings: light usage (~100 reqs/min) for semantic search; not the majority.

As questions for you:
1) What GPU pool configuration would you recommend (type and count) to hit the steady-state + burst profile while keeping typical p95 latency in that target range?
2) How do you price burst credits vs reserved capacity? Any caps or throttling approach during sustained bursts?
3) What discount/packaging would you propose for an initial 12-month commit vs 24-month commit?

If useful I can pass along a small sample of traffic traces (anonymized) — we want an honest sizing with clear overage rules so our infra team can sign off. Can we do a short call this week to walk the numbers?

Best,
Jordan Park
Head of Platform
OptimaAI
+1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool sizing & flexible commit options

Jordan — thanks for the clear signal. We can absolutely model this out. Quick, high-level notes (preliminary):

- For Llama-3-70B quantized workloads the throughput per H100 (full precision kernels optimized for long context) is roughly 6–10 req/s at 1200 tokens with p95 ~200–300ms depending on batching and KV-cache reuse. A100 80GB with optimized kernels will be somewhat lower for long contexts.
- Given your steady 25 req/s and burst profile to 140 req/s, a safe initial recommendation would be an 8-instance H100 pool (balanced across 2 availability zones) with automated burst credits and autoscale buffer. That provides headroom for bursts without violating latency SLOs and keeps tail latency predictable.
- Alternative conservative config: 6x H100 + aggressive KV caching and prefix caching in front for the 90% short-path requests — may save 15–25% cost but requires integration work.

I'm attaching a quick model workbook with a couple of scenarios (steady, burst, and conservative). Please review the "steady vs burst" tab and confirm the percent of requests that are long-context (>2k tokens) vs short (<800 tokens). That number changes recommended pool size materially.

On pricing & packaging: we have two levers — reserved monthly commit and burst credits. Reservations give you a predictable unit price with a graduated discount by commit length; burst credits are pre-purchased or can be used as an overage pool with defined throttles after credits are consumed. I cc'd Ben (pricing) and Karthik (ops) to lay out a clean proposal and draft MSA.

Can we target a 30-minute sizing call tomorrow at 10am PT?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Sales Manager, Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Evelyn/Team — quick follow-up after internal check:
- Long-context (>2k tokens) requests are ~18% of traffic, short (<800 tokens) are ~62%, rest are medium (~20%).
- Burst pattern: mostly start-of-business spikes and some weekly marketing-driven campaigns that produce the 15–30 minute bursts.
- Embeddings traffic is mostly offloaded to a separate, lower-cost pool but we may want a small shared quota on the dedicated pool for read-latency sensitive calls.
- Optima is evaluating two providers; pricing and guaranteed throughput matter a lot. The competitor offered a 12-month reserved option with 12% discount + a fixed burst bundle. Curious if Redwood can improve that — particularly for committed monthly spend above $180k.

We'll join the call tomorrow at 10am PT. Also attaching anonymized request histogram for your modeling team.

Jordan

Subject: Re: Inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool sizing & flexible commit options

Jordan — great to meet on the call this morning and thanks for the histogram. Below is a concise proposal based on the traffic mix you provided and our ops assumptions:

Recommended capacity (baseline):
- 8x H100 nodes (dedicated pool), split across two AZs for availability. Expected steady throughput: ~48–64 req/s (with batching + KV reuse) and burst handling to ~160 req/s using pre-warmed burst buffers + short-path cache.
- Optional 2x A100 as a lower-cost overflow tier for non-latency-critical, long-generation jobs.

Pricing summary (monthly, USD):
- 12-month reserved commit: $174,000 / month (base) — includes 500k burst credits / month and 24/7 support. Standard discount applied.
- 24-month reserved commit: $148,000 / month (base) — includes 750k burst credits / month and higher priority for capacity expansions.
- Overage: If monthly usage exceeds reserved capacity + burst credits, overage billed at $0.32 per additional GPU-minute equivalent, with automatic throttle thresholds at 110% sustained for >2 hours.
- Special: For deals >$2M ARR we can offer an additional one-time onboarding credit and a 3% prepayment discount.

Guarantees & SLAs:
- Latency SLO: p95 response within 300ms for requests <= 1.5k tokens under committed capacity. Longer contexts have a best-effort SLO and will be routed to the overflow tier if needed.
- Throughput: We guarantee steady-state throughput within 95% of modeled numbers; we provide rollback to a compatible smaller model variant as a fallback to preserve availability in extreme conditions.

Next steps:
1) We will circulate a redlineable MSA and the capacity costing workbook (attached).
2) If you confirm the 12 vs 24 month preference, we will prepare an internal capacity reservation and a DocuSign packet.

Attachments: draft_msa_redwood_optimaai_v1.pdf

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben/Evelyn — the numbers look reasonable and materially competitive vs the other quote. A couple of final asks before we move to PO:
1) Can you increase the included burst credits in the 12-month plan to 650k / month (we can commit to a quarterly usage review) in exchange for an electronic PO within 10 business days?
2) Can we get explicit language in Section 5 of the MSA about overage throttling thresholds (we prefer a soft-stepped throttle vs hard cut-off)?

If you can accommodate those two items we'll route for internal sign-off and expect to issue a PO within the requested window. Happy to take a short call if needed.

Jordan Park
Head of Platform
OptimaAI
